title: Choose the SHUAMO catalog structure
question: All three keep SHUAMO's ink, paper and signal-indigo visual system. Choose how creators should browse products and understand the complete affiliate offer.

options.label: Product Passports
options.lineage: product passport and commercial offer sheet
options.thesis: Every product reads as a complete, trustworthy offer before a creator opens it.
options.viewport: Wide image-led rows pair category, description and brand with a right-aligned commission and terms snapshot; the detail page becomes a gallery-led product passport with a sticky offer panel.
options.risk: Rows are taller than a table, so brand management needs a compact-density toggle for large catalogs.

options.label: Deal Desk
options.lineage: professional media browser with a live inspector
options.thesis: Creators compare products without losing their place, while full details remain one selection away.
options.viewport: A searchable product list occupies the left, a large active photograph the center, and commission, eligibility and actions form a persistent inspector on the right; phones transition cleanly from list to detail.
options.risk: The three-pane desktop is highly efficient but requires careful focus management and a simpler mobile navigation model.

options.label: Category Gallery
options.lineage: curated retail collection with rigorous offer metadata
options.thesis: Fixed product types become the primary way to explore a visually rich marketplace.
options.viewport: A strong category navigator leads into a responsive image grid; each card shows brand, product type, price and commission, while the detail page opens into an immersive gallery with the full terms below a sticky summary.
options.risk: This is the most attractive browsing experience but slower than the other options for bulk comparison and brand operations.
